title: Macaroni or Pasta Salad with Shrimp

content.title: About
content.content: Macaroni or pasta salad with shrimp is a cold dish that combines cooked pasta, boiled or sautéed shrimp, fresh vegetables, and a light dressing made from mayonnaise, yogurt or olive oil. The salad offers a delicate seafood flavor, aromatic herbs, and a pleasant texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Short‑shaped pasta such as shells, penne or fusilli is usually used to hold the dressing better.
Shrimp are high‑protein and low‑calorie, making the salad diet‑friendly.
The classic recipe appeared in the United States in the 1970s as a light summer side.
Adding fresh herbs (parsley, dill, basil) boosts aroma and nutritional value.
The salad can be prepared ahead of time and retains its taste for up to 24 hours in the fridge.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Shrimp provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: The dish combines modest fat and calorie levels, suitable for weight management.

items.title: Source of omega‑3
items.content: Shrimp contain small amounts of omega‑3 fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Shrimp are a good source of vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Whole‑grain pasta (if used) provides dietary fiber that promotes regular bowel function.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Shrimp are a common allergen; individuals with shellfish allergy should avoid this dish.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol; people with hypercholesterolemia should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Sodium in dressing
items.content: Prepared mayonnaise‑based or soy dressings can be high in sodium; control added salt.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Shrimp must be fully cooked; raw seafood may harbor pathogens.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish or as a side to fish and meat. It is easy to eat with a fork or spoon and can also be used as a sandwich filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 2 days. Stir before serving to redistribute the dressing.
